criteria.text: `openTeamDb` on an empty directory creates `team.db` at team schema 1 with the tables above, mints `server.id`, `server.instance`, `server.created_at` and `team.schema`, and a second open changes nothing; a file at a newer team version is refused with `SchemaTooNewError`; a client store's file renamed `team.db`, and a file with a version and no `meta` table, are refused as "not a team database" before any migration runs, by `openTeamDb` and by `openTeamExisting` alike; `openDb` on a client store still applies `MIGRATIONS` and the module schemas as before, closes its handle when a module migration fails, restricts the files after both migrations, and its upgrade copies, the module schemas' included, still land in its own `backups/`; `openExisting` keeps its `allowNewer` and its busy timeout (the runner's split changes no behaviour); the way back across a bump holds: with a two-migration list `openFile` leaves `backups/team-<ms>-v1-<pid>.db`, the version-1 list then refuses the file with `SchemaTooNewError`, after the copy is put in place with `team.db-wal` and `team.db-shm` removed the version-1 list opens it, and a `feed.seq` ahead of it makes `checkRestore` renew the instance, advance the sequence (the `sqlite_sequence` row inserted when absent) and rewrite the file; the viewer's `json`, `problem` and `jsonObject` live in `src/http/respond.ts` and the viewer's tests pass unchanged; `setLogSink` routes `logError` to the sink and, unset, to the file as before; `gitEnv` and `runGit` take a `GitHost` that part 1's store satisfies as it is, a per-call `timeoutMs` keeps its precedence over the host's, the staging and commit helpers take a repository path and `commitPaths` a `committer`, part 1's tests pass unchanged, and `gitEnv` with a `committer` sets the committer variables apart from the author's.

every other route is 401 without a token, 403 `member disabled` for a disabled member's device (its devices revoked as well), 401 `device revoked` for a revoked device of an active member, each with `serverId` and `instance` in the body; `join` with the bootstrap code and `name: "André"` makes an admin named `André` (absent, `admin`) and answers a `wcm1_` token once with the device's id and alias, `serverId` and `instance`, and the same code again is 410 `invitation used`; `join` with an unknown, expired or revoked code is 404 or 410 and audited with the address and without the code, and a rate-limited address writes no audit row; a label over 80 characters or a bad name is 400; the eleventh join from one address in a minute is 429 with `Retry-After`; the 601st request of a device in a minute is 429, a held pull counts once, and an item that would take a device's applied payload past 64 MiB in an hour is `refused rate` while an idempotent retry is not charged; with `trustProxy` the address is the last `X-Forwarded-For` hop, an authenticated request without `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` is 400, and a `join` without it is 400 `https required` and spends no invitation; `GET /v1/me` answers the member, the device with its alias, `serverId`, `instance`, `contract: 1` and the limits (`pullWaitSeconds` 25 and `payloadBytesPerHour` among them); every answer the handler gives carries `X-Request-Id`, a client's valid `X-Request-Id` is echoed, a `Content-Length` above 1 MiB and a chunked body past 1 MiB are 413 with a request id, and a thrown error answers `{ error: "internal error", requestId }` with the message in a log line of the same id.

an admin's `POST /v1/invitations { role: "member", name: "Ana Lopes" }` makes a code a new member joins with, a name of 81 characters or beginning `agent:` is 400, and `expiresInHours` outside 1 to 720 is 400; `{ forMember }` makes a code that adds a device to that member and `GET /v1/me` on both devices shows one member id; a member calling any invitation or admin route is 403; `GET /v1/invitations` lists unused ones; `POST /v1/invitations/<id>/revoke` makes the code 410 `invitation revoked`; revoking a device cancels its unused invitations; the last active admin's disable, device revoke or demotion is 409 `the last admin stays` with a `hint`; `POST /v1/members/<id>/role { role: "admin" }` promotes; `POST /v1/members/<id>/disable { withdraw: true }` revokes the member's devices and tombstones their workspace entries and their devices' memories with one feed row each and no lock, and leaves a shared entry they created untouched; `POST /v1/members/<id>/enable` clears the disable, a device invitation joins the member again under the same id, and their re-send of a tombstoned workspace entry on the tombstone's base applies; `POST /v1/items/entry/<uid>/withdraw` with a URL-encoded project uid tombstones and locks and answers the revision, on an already withdrawn item it locks alone, `reinstate` unlocks and the owner's re-send then applies; every admin action and every CLI write writes an audit row (`source` `api` or `cli`), and the plan's route table's shapes and statuses hold for every admin route.

decisions.question: Where does the server keep its data: its own SQLite database and git repositories under its data directory, or a client's store schema reused on the server?
decisions.default: Its own: a team database with its own migrations and one git repository per server scope under the data directory, never a client's store. The server's shape is the team's, not one machine's; a client's schema carries sessions, turns and hooks the server must never hold.

decisions.question: How are device tokens made and stored: random high-entropy secrets hashed at rest, or a password-style secret hashed with a slow function?
decisions.default: A device token is 32 random bytes, shown once at join, stored as its SHA-256 digest only and compared in constant time; a high-entropy secret needs no slow hash, and a leaked database holds nothing that logs in. Revocation deletes nothing: revoked_at is set and the device refused.

decisions.question: How is the first admin created: a one-time invitation the server prints at its first start, or a secret passed on the command line or in the environment?
decisions.default: A one-time admin invitation minted at the first start with an empty database, printed once to standard output and written to a 0600 file in the data directory that is deleted when used, valid for 24 hours; nothing else answers until it is used. A secret in a flag or the environment would land in shell history and compose files.
decisions.answer: o resto concordo com tudo (default aceite) (the person's answer of 2026-11-10 to this same question on item 2026-11-09-003, relayed)

decisions.question: What is an invitation: a single-use code with a role and an expiry made by an admin, or an open sign-up or an e-mail flow?
decisions.default: A single-use code of 128 bits (26 base32 characters) with a role and an expiry of 72 hours by default, made by an admin through the API or the server's CLI, stored hashed, consumed by one join; no open sign-up, no e-mail: the admin hands the code over however the team talks.
decisions.answer: o resto concordo com tudo (default aceite) (the person's answer of 2026-11-10 to this same question on item 2026-11-09-003, relayed)

decisions.question: What may each role do, and can the last admin be removed?
decisions.default: A member pushes and pulls and sees every item of the server's one destination; an admin does the same and also creates invitations, lists members and devices, revokes a device, disables a member and withdraws any item; the last active admin cannot be revoked, disabled or demoted. Two roles only in this part.
decisions.answer: o resto concordo com tudo (default aceite) (the person's answer of 2026-11-10 to this same question on item 2026-11-09-003, relayed)

decisions.question: What is the sync API's shape: JSON over HTTP under a versioned prefix with a batch push answering per item and a pull by a monotonic cursor, or another transport?
decisions.default: JSON over HTTP under /v1/: the push route takes up to 200 items with the client's policy epoch and answers each item applied, stale with the server's current version and hash, refused with a reason code from a fixed list, or withdrawn; the pull route takes the last sequence seen and answers the changes after it, 500 at most, with the next cursor and whether more follow; bodies capped at 1 MiB; a per-device rate limit of 600 requests a minute answered 429 with Retry-After. The same shape part 4's decide and ledger speak.
decisions.answer: sim (default aceite, mais o wait da D-22 na rota de pull) (the person's answer of 2026-11-10 to this same question on item 2026-11-09-003, relayed)

decisions.question: How is a conflict decided: an entry push carries the base version and hash it was made from and a mismatch is refused with the server's current ones, while memories belong to one device; or last write wins?
decisions.default: Versions decide, never a silent overwrite: an entry push carries both the base version and the base hash the client built on; the server applies it only when both equal its current ones, else answers stale with the current version and hash; a first send of an unknown entry carries base version 0. A memory belongs to the device that first sent its uid: that device replaces or withdraws it, another device's push of the same uid is refused.

decisions.question: What does the server store from a pushed item, and how does it check the shape?
decisions.default: Exactly part 4's payload types, OutgoingEntry and OutgoingMemory, plus the member, the device, the server's version, the hash and the times; the payload is checked at the boundary against the key lists part 4's contract test pins, so an unknown or missing field is refused with the reason shape and adding a field changes both sides together. The server never asks for, and never keeps, anything else.

decisions.question: How does a second machine join as the same member, and what identifies a device?
decisions.default: An invitation may be bound to an existing member: an admin makes one for a member, or the member makes one from a device they already hold; a join with a bound invitation adds a device to that member, a join with an unbound one creates a member. A device id is an independent random value (12 base32 characters), never derived from the token, so a token can be rotated without changing the id.

decisions.question: Which store is the authority for an applied item, and how do the git repositories relate to it?
decisions.default: The team database is the authority: a push is applied in one transaction that stores the payload bytes as sent, the server's version, the hash, the owner and a change-feed row, and answers; the git repositories are a versioned mirror written after the commit by one in-process queue, one commit per applied item with the member as author and the server as committer, and a row still pending at start is mirrored then. The mission puts the repositories on the volume for the team's history; the sync never reads them.

decisions.question: What does a device pull: every item of the server, or the shared and workspace knowledge plus the project items of the projects that machine works on?
decisions.default: The shared repository's and the members' workspace entries always, and project-scoped entries and memories only for the remote aliases the device names in its pull; so a laptop never holds a project it does not work on, which is ADR 0018's rule carried across people. The pull answers one current row per uid since the cursor, tombstones included within their retention, 500 items or 2 MiB per page.

decisions.question: Who may write and withdraw which items on the server?
decisions.default: A shared or project entry is the team's: any member may push a new version on the current base, and the last writer is recorded; a member's workspace entry is written only by that member's devices; a memory is replaced only by the device that first sent it, applied only when its updatedAt is not older than the stored one. A withdraw is accepted from a device of the item's last writer, or from an admin; another member's withdraw is refused not-owner.
